title: One Point Lesson - Nitrogen Blanketing (PCV-8905) (OPL-FA-8901-04)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-FA-8901-04 - Nitrogen Blanketing (PCV-8905).

Equipment: FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 8900 - HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-8901 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-8901.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains nitrogen blanketing (pcv-8905) for FA-8901 (REFLUX ACCUMULATOR DRUM) in the HEXANE COLUMN OVERHEAD SYSTEM. The nitrogen blanket keeps air out of the hexane drum and holds a stable pressure; loss of blanket risks an explosive atmosphere. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Verify the PCV-8905 split-range holds PT-8902 pressure
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Confirm the blanket makes up on falling pressure
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Confirm the vent relieves on rising pressure
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Respond immediately to a blanket-loss alarm
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Check the N2 supply header pressure is adequate
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Reflux drum level transmitter drifting vs gauge | Likely Cause: Transmitter zero drift | Action: Recalibrated LT-8901 against the bridle gauge
- Symptom: Statutory relief valve test | Likely Cause: Set pressure drift found | Action: Overhauled PSV-8901, lapped seat, re-set 10 barg, certified
- Symptom: Boot drain valve N4 passing / leaking | Likely Cause: Seat eroded by water/solids | Action: Reseated / replaced boot drain valve HV-8904

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The nitrogen blanket keeps air out of the hexane drum and holds a stable pressure; loss of blanket risks an explosive atmosphere.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-8901: e.g. LSHH-8901 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-8901 before working on FA-8901.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
